answer: Not done, deliberately. The project holds no storm-sewer data: data/raw/flood_ida has only the USGS high-water-mark CSV, its dictionary and 3DEP elevation tiles. The only 'storm' text matches are notes like 'car has not been moved since the storm'. pro/flood_ida.py is a terrain-only screen (fill-sink depth and TPI sampled at marks and random controls); it has no hydraulic or drainage component and no depth prediction to adjust. Adding sewer capacity would need NYC DEP sewer/catchment data (not fetched) and rainfall input, or invented capacity values, which the rules forbid. So I cannot report an improvement in match with the high-water marks; any such number would be fabricated.
traps_or_caveats: No storm-sewer layer (pipe diameters, catchment, capacity) exists in data/raw; would need to be sourced (e.g. NYC DEP/NYC Open Data) and added to the catalog, not assumed.

Model is a terrain low-spot screen (sink depth, TPI), not a hydrodynamic model; sewer capacity cannot be 'added' to it without building a rainfall-runoff/drainage model, and no rainfall input is in the data.
Baseline-vs-with-sewer improvement requires running the pro scripts and scoring, which was prohibited here; no existing metric was read or quoted.

HWMs are a mix of riverine/coastal and interior marks (basement, etc.) and measure height above ground at survey; pluvial sewer-overflow flooding may be only part of them, so sewer capacity should only be expected to explain a subset.
3DEP DEM is bare-earth at ~2 m: culverts, sewer inlets and depressions under bridges are not represented, and sink depth overstates ponding where sewers drain.
Any 'improvement' obtained with guessed capacities would be circular/misleading.
